questions.stem: How should the agent's loop decide whether to keep calling tools?

options.text: Always run exactly three iterations
Stop when the reply text contains the word "resolved"
Stop as soon as a response has no text block
Continue while `stop_reason` is `tool_use`, returning tool results each time, and finish when it is `end_turn`

questions.explanation: `stop_reason` is the model's own signal: `tool_use` means run the tool and continue, `end_turn` means it has finished.

distractor_notes.A: A fixed count cuts long tasks short and wastes calls on short ones.
distractor_notes.B: Text matching is brittle; the model may phrase completion differently or mention the word mid-task.
distractor_notes.C: A tool call can have no text yet still need its result returned.

questions.stem: The loop can end unexpectedly (timeout, iteration cap, repeated tool failure). Which design best guarantees every conversation still ends in a resolution or a documented handoff?

options.text: A system-prompt instruction to always resolve or escalate before stopping
Retry the loop indefinitely until the model resolves the case
Log the failure and close the conversation
A guard in the orchestration code that checks for a terminal state on every exit path and, if none exists, escalates to a human with a summary of what happened

questions.explanation: Guarantees belong in code that runs regardless of how the loop terminates, not in model behaviour.

distractor_notes.A: It is advisory and cannot help when the loop exits abnormally.
distractor_notes.B: Unbounded retries hang the customer and hide the failure.
distractor_notes.C: The customer is left without a resolution or handoff.

questions.stem: `get_order` currently returns the text "Error" for both a missing order and a backend outage, and the agent tells customers their order does not exist during outages. What should the tool return?

options.text: The raw stack trace as text
A longer generic message such as "Something went wrong"
An error flagged `isError` with a category (not_found vs transient), whether it is retryable and a suggested next action
An empty result for both cases

questions.explanation: Typed errors let the agent retry transient failures and report genuine not-found cases correctly.

distractor_notes.A: It is noisy and gives no explicit recoverability.
distractor_notes.B: Still no category, so the agent cannot choose between retrying and reporting.
distractor_notes.D: It makes an outage look like a legitimate "no such order".

questions.stem: The team wants a reusable `/triage-ticket` command that every developer on the repository can invoke on demand. Where should it live?

options.text: In each developer's `~/.claude/commands/`
As a Markdown file in the project's `.claude/commands/` directory, committed to the repository
In `.claude/settings.json` under `permissions`
In CLAUDE.md as a paragraph of instructions

questions.explanation: Project commands in `.claude/commands/` are shared through version control; user commands in `~/.claude/commands/` are personal.

distractor_notes.A: That is personal to one machine and would not reach teammates.
distractor_notes.C: Permissions gate tools; they do not define commands.
distractor_notes.D: CLAUDE.md is always-loaded context, not an on-demand command.

questions.stem: The team must add a new escalation policy engine touching about twelve modules, with the compliance group reviewing the approach first. How should they use Claude Code?

options.text: Use `bypassPermissions` so the change finishes faster
Execute directly and review the resulting diff afterwards
Ask for the code changes in small steps with no plan
Start in plan mode to explore read-only and produce a plan for review, then implement after approval

questions.explanation: Large scope, uncertainty and stakeholder review call for plan mode; small reversible edits suit direct execution.

distractor_notes.A: It removes safeguards on a broad, sensitive change.
distractor_notes.B: The compliance review is needed before implementation, and a large change is costly to unwind.
distractor_notes.C: The architectural approach still needs sign-off first.

questions.stem: Every incoming message must be classified into an intent object that downstream code reads from a tool call. Which configuration guarantees that?

options.text: Leave `tool_choice` as `auto` and add a reminder to use the tool
Ask for JSON in the system prompt
Set `tool_choice` to `none` and parse the reply
Define a classification tool with a JSON schema and set `tool_choice` to force that tool

questions.explanation: Forcing a schema-backed tool guarantees a tool call whose input matches the schema.

distractor_notes.A: Auto lets the model answer in text, which would break the parser.
distractor_notes.B: Prompt-based formatting has no guarantee.
distractor_notes.C: That prevents tool calls entirely.

questions.stem: A customer writes, "I want to speak to a person now." The agent could resolve the refund itself in one step. What should it do?

options.text: Complete the refund first to show it can help
Offer to keep trying twice before escalating
Ask the customer to explain why they want a human
Honor the request immediately: escalate with a summary of the conversation so far

questions.explanation: An explicit human-escalation request is honored at once; autonomous resolution is for cases without such a request.

distractor_notes.A: It overrides an explicit request from the customer.
distractor_notes.B: An explicit request should not be bargained down.
distractor_notes.C: It delays and frustrates a clear request.

questions.stem: Some invoices carry no purchase-order number, yet `po_number` is a required string and the model sometimes invents one. What is the best schema change?

options.text: Drop the field and have staff enter it
Keep it required and add "do not guess" to the prompt
Use the placeholder `"UNKNOWN"` when missing
Make `po_number` nullable and tell the model to return null when the document has none

questions.explanation: Allow the model to report absence truthfully with null or an optional field.

distractor_notes.A: It discards the value for the invoices that do have one.
distractor_notes.B: The schema still demands a value, so guessing remains the easiest way to comply.
distractor_notes.C: A placeholder is indistinguishable from data downstream.

questions.stem: When a low-confidence extraction goes to an analyst, which TWO items belong in the handoff package? (Select 2)

options.text: A reference to the source document and page, plus which automated checks already ran
The model's complete raw reasoning transcript
A one-line note saying "please review"
The extracted values with per-field confidence and the reason each uncertain field is uncertain

questions.explanation: A good handoff is structured and complete enough that the receiver need not redo the work.

distractor_notes.B: It buries the useful facts in noise.
distractor_notes.C: It drops the context the analyst needs to act quickly.

questions.stem: Some contract bundles include amendments that refer to other contracts not yet retrieved. The current fixed extraction sequence misses those references. What design fits best?

options.text: Ask analysts to add referenced contracts by hand
An orchestrator that plans subtasks from what it finds and adds retrieval and extraction steps for referenced contracts as they appear
Add more fixed steps for every kind of reference, run on every document
Merge all steps into one long prompt

questions.explanation: When the next step depends on findings, generate subtasks dynamically.

distractor_notes.A: It moves the adaptive planning to people.
distractor_notes.C: It wastes work on most documents and still misses unknown patterns.
distractor_notes.D: It cannot adapt to what each step discovers.

questions.stem: `get_vendor_profile` needs a `vendor_id` returned by `match_vendor`. The model sometimes calls it with a guessed id. What is the most reliable fix?

options.text: Set `tool_choice` to `any` on every turn
Make the dependency explicit in code (the profile tool only accepts an id issued by `match_vendor`) and describe it in the tool descriptions
Rename `get_vendor_profile` to `get_vendor_profile_second`
Add "call match_vendor first" to the system prompt only

questions.explanation: Prerequisite data is best enforced programmatically, with the dependency documented for the model.

distractor_notes.A: It forces a tool call each turn but does not order them, and prevents a final answer.
distractor_notes.C: A name is a hint, not enforcement.
distractor_notes.D: Advice alone can still be ignored.

questions.stem: The agent confuses `extract_invoice` and `extract_contract`, whose descriptions both read "Extract fields from a document." How should the tools be improved?

options.text: Delete one tool and use a single generic extractor
Rename them `tool1` and `tool2`
Tell the model in the system prompt to choose carefully
Rewrite each description to say what document type it handles, give example inputs, and state when not to use it

questions.explanation: Selection depends on descriptions that state purpose, inputs and disambiguation.

distractor_notes.A: It loses the type-specific behaviour.
distractor_notes.B: Names without meaning make selection worse.
distractor_notes.C: It gives no criteria to choose by.

questions.stem: A developer asks Claude Code to improve date normalisation, but it still fails on several formats. Which follow-up is most effective?

options.text: Repeat the original request more forcefully
Clear the session and start over each time
Say "try harder"
Provide concrete input/expected-output examples for the failing formats, ideally as tests, and send them together

questions.explanation: Concrete examples and batched feedback let the model converge.

distractor_notes.A: It adds no information about what is wrong.
distractor_notes.B: It discards the feedback gathered so far.
distractor_notes.C: Effort words do not describe the failure.

questions.stem: Analysts spend most of their time on records that turn out correct. How should records be routed to review?

options.text: A random 5% of all records
By per-field confidence and document characteristics, with thresholds calibrated on a labelled sample
Everything from newly onboarded vendors
The longest documents first

questions.explanation: Route scarce review effort to where errors are likely, validated on labelled data.

distractor_notes.A: Most reviewed records would still be fine.
distractor_notes.C: A crude proxy that ignores which fields are risky.
distractor_notes.D: Length is a weak signal.

questions.stem: An engineer resumes yesterday's session, but a teammate changed several analysed files overnight. What is the best way to continue?

options.text: Delete the earlier analysis and restart the migration plan
Continue as if nothing changed
Start a brand-new session and re-read the whole repository
Resume the session, tell Claude which files changed, and have it re-analyse just those files before continuing

questions.explanation: Session resumption works best with targeted re-analysis of what changed.

distractor_notes.A: It discards valid findings about unchanged files.
distractor_notes.B: Earlier conclusions about those files may now be wrong.
distractor_notes.C: It repeats work already done.

questions.stem: A `dependency-graph` server was added to the project's `.mcp.json`. How can the developer confirm it is connected and its tools are available?

options.text: Edit CLAUDE.md to mention the server
Ask the model whether it thinks the tools exist
Check `/mcp` in Claude Code to see the server's status and discovered tools
Restart the machine and see if it works

questions.explanation: `/mcp` shows connection status and the tools discovered.

distractor_notes.A: CLAUDE.md does not register servers.
distractor_notes.B: The model may guess; `/mcp` reports the actual state.
distractor_notes.D: It does not tell you whether the server connected.

questions.stem: Which of these tasks is best done directly rather than in plan mode?

options.text: Splitting the billing module into a new service
Replacing the persistence framework across all modules
Choosing service boundaries for the whole monolith
Renaming one private method and its two call sites, with tests passing before and after

questions.explanation: Small, reversible, well-scoped work suits direct execution.

distractor_notes.A: Large, uncertain and hard to reverse; plan first.
distractor_notes.B: Broad scope needing review before implementation.
distractor_notes.C: Architectural uncertainty is high.

questions.stem: The team must guarantee Claude never runs `git push --force`. Which mechanism is right?

options.text: A `permissions.deny` rule for `Bash(git push --force:*)` in the project's `.claude/settings.json`
A rule in `.claude/rules/` scoped to `**/*.java`
A Skill describing safe git usage
A sentence in CLAUDE.md saying never to force-push

questions.explanation: Guarantees come from enforced settings or hooks, not from context.

distractor_notes.B: Rules are context and this action is not tied to Java files.
distractor_notes.C: Skills load at the model's discretion.
distractor_notes.D: CLAUDE.md is advisory and can be ignored.

questions.stem: A script classifies 4,000 stored procedures into migration categories and loads the result into a tracker that rejects malformed JSON. Which method is most reliable?

options.text: Prefill the reply with `{`
A tool with a JSON schema for the classification, with `tool_choice` forcing it
Post-process replies with regexes
Prompt the model to return only JSON

questions.explanation: Schema-backed tool use gives the strongest structural guarantee.

distractor_notes.A: It starts the output but does not enforce the schema.
distractor_notes.C: It is brittle and misses missing keys.
distractor_notes.D: No schema guarantee.

questions.stem: The classifier keeps mislabelling some procedures. How should the team use the errors to improve results?

options.text: Retrain the underlying model on the errors
Record structured metadata for each error (predicted category, correct category, reason) and use the patterns to refine the prompt, schema or few-shot examples
Ignore errors below 5%
Add one special-case sentence per error

questions.explanation: Structured error capture turns failures into targeted prompt and example improvements.

distractor_notes.A: Users of the API cannot retrain the model; they improve prompts and examples.
distractor_notes.C: Patterns in errors are the input for improvement.
distractor_notes.D: Accumulated special cases cause regressions.

questions.stem: You must find every place the `ORDERS` table is written to, in a repository with vendored and generated code. What is the best approach?

options.text: Glob everything and read whatever looks important
Grep for the table name and write-related patterns with path filters that exclude vendored and generated code, then Read only the relevant ranges
Read every file in the data-access package in full
Grep the whole repository unfiltered and read every hit

questions.explanation: Search narrowly, then read targeted ranges.

distractor_notes.A: Names are a poor guide to content.
distractor_notes.C: It consumes context on irrelevant code.
distractor_notes.D: Vendored and generated matches flood the context.

questions.stem: The `deploy` MCP tool must never run against production without an approved change ticket, a rule set by the business, not left to the model. What should enforce it?

options.text: A PreToolUse hook that checks the ticket and blocks the call (exit code 2) when it is missing
A PostToolUse hook that rolls back a deployment when no ticket exists
A note in the tool description asking the model to check for a ticket
A line in CLAUDE.md about change tickets

questions.explanation: Business rules that must always hold are enforced in a PreToolUse hook that runs before the tool.

distractor_notes.B: The deployment has already happened.
distractor_notes.C: The model could still call it.
distractor_notes.D: It is advisory.

questions.stem: The team wants the ticketing server shared by everyone who clones the repo, while one engineer wants a personal experimental server across all their projects. Which scopes?

options.text: Both at local scope
Ticketing at user scope and the experiment at project scope
Both at project scope
Ticketing at project scope in `.mcp.json`; the experimental server at user scope

questions.explanation: Shared tooling is project scope; personal or experimental servers are user scope.

distractor_notes.A: Local is private to one developer in one project, so nothing is shared.
distractor_notes.B: The scopes are reversed.
distractor_notes.C: A personal experiment would be imposed on the whole team.

questions.stem: The feature-flag server is rate limited. What should its tool return so the agent waits and retries once?

options.text: HTTP status 429 only
An error with category `rate_limit`, `retryable: true`, a retry-after value and a suggested action
An empty list
The text "failed"

questions.explanation: Actionable error metadata drives correct recovery.

distractor_notes.A: The agent must infer policy and timing.
distractor_notes.C: It looks like a valid empty result.
distractor_notes.D: It carries no cause or recoverability.

questions.stem: `set_flag` takes an `environment` argument, and the model passes "production" or "prod" or "PROD" inconsistently, failing validation. What is the best fix?

options.text: Accept any string and lowercase it server-side without documenting it
Add "be consistent" to the system prompt
Rename the parameter to `env_name`
Document the accepted values in the parameter description and constrain the parameter with an enum

questions.explanation: Explicit formats and enums in the tool definition steer argument values.

distractor_notes.A: It hides the contract and the model still guesses.
distractor_notes.B: It gives no concrete values.
distractor_notes.C: A rename does not say which values are valid.

questions.stem: Guidance to prefer the flag MCP tools over shell commands matters only when files under `services/flags/` are involved. Which mechanism fits?

options.text: The root CLAUDE.md for every session
A `permissions.allow` entry
A PostToolUse hook that prints the guidance after each edit
A `.claude/rules/` file with a `paths` glob for `services/flags/**`

questions.explanation: Path-specific guidance belongs in path-scoped rules.

distractor_notes.A: It would load the guidance where it is irrelevant.
distractor_notes.B: Permissions do not carry guidance.
distractor_notes.C: Hooks react to tool events, not to a topic.

questions.stem: The chat assistant usually converses, but when the user asks for a deployment plan it must produce a schema-valid plan object. What is the best design?

options.text: Use `none` and ask for JSON text
Force `submit_plan` on every request
Always use `any` and read whichever tool is called
Use `auto` for normal chat and, for plan requests, force a `submit_plan` tool with a JSON schema

questions.explanation: Force the schema tool only for the step that needs guaranteed structure.

distractor_notes.A: No schema guarantee and no tool call.
distractor_notes.B: The assistant could no longer chat.
distractor_notes.C: It would force a tool call even for casual chat.

questions.stem: The API conventions document is needed in nearly every session, while a one-off migration spec is needed only for a single task. How should each be provided?

options.text: Both in CLAUDE.md permanently
Conventions inline each time; the spec in CLAUDE.md
Both by asking Claude to remember them
Conventions via CLAUDE.md (or an import from it); the one-off spec via an `@` file reference in that task's prompt

questions.explanation: Use persistent memory for recurring context and explicit references for task-specific context.

distractor_notes.A: The transient spec would clutter every session.
distractor_notes.B: The roles are reversed, wasting effort and context.
distractor_notes.C: Nothing persists across sessions on its own.

questions.stem: When the coordinator invokes the analysis subagent, which TWO things must it pass explicitly? (Select 2)

options.text: The coordinator's entire raw history, automatically attached
Nothing beyond the task title, because the subagent inherits the coordinator's context
The task, plus the relevant findings gathered so far
Constraints and the expected output format

questions.explanation: A subagent knows only what is placed in its prompt, so hand it what it needs in a structured form.

distractor_notes.A: Nothing is attached automatically, and dumping everything wastes context.
distractor_notes.B: Subagents run in their own context and do not inherit it.

questions.stem: After the first round of searches shows the question is really about two different market segments, the plan should change. What design supports that?

options.text: A fixed three-step pipeline
Repeat the same search with different wording until it works
The coordinator generates and revises subtasks from intermediate findings and delegates them
One long prompt covering all possibilities

questions.explanation: Open-ended research needs dynamic decomposition.

distractor_notes.A: It cannot adapt to findings.
distractor_notes.B: It does not restructure the work.
distractor_notes.D: It removes checkpoints and adaptability.

questions.stem: The coordinator's response has three `tool_use` blocks for three subagent calls. How should the results be returned?

options.text: Run all three and send all three `tool_result` blocks back together in one user message
Ignore the calls and continue the conversation
Send each result in its own user message
Return only the first result

questions.explanation: Return every result for the assistant turn together.

distractor_notes.B: The model is waiting for the results.
distractor_notes.C: Results for one assistant turn belong in one message.
distractor_notes.D: The other calls would be left without results and the API rejects that.

questions.stem: `analyse_document` needs a `doc_id` from `search_documents`, and the model sometimes calls both in parallel with a guessed id. What helps most?

options.text: Retry the analysis until it succeeds
Set `tool_choice` to `any`
Disable parallel tool use and document the dependency so the search result is available before the analysis call
Shorten the tool names

questions.explanation: Dependent calls must wait for the earlier result.

distractor_notes.A: It hides a design flaw and wastes calls.
distractor_notes.B: It does not order the calls.
distractor_notes.D: It has no effect on ordering.

questions.stem: An analyst wants a personal `/summarise-sources` command available in all of their projects but not shared with the team. Where does it belong?

options.text: In the project's `.claude/commands/`
In `.mcp.json`
In CLAUDE.md
In `~/.claude/commands/` as a Markdown file

questions.explanation: User-level commands are personal and follow you across projects.

distractor_notes.A: It would be shared with everyone who clones the repository.
distractor_notes.B: That file configures MCP servers.
distractor_notes.C: That is context, not a command.

questions.stem: The coordinator's context fills with raw pages from twenty sources. What is the best way to keep it usable?

options.text: Have subagents read the sources in their own contexts and return concise findings, and record key findings in a notes file
Rely on `/compact` alone
Paste every source into the coordinator so nothing is lost
Read only the first source and assume the rest agree

questions.explanation: Isolate noisy reading in subagents and persist durable findings.

distractor_notes.B: Summaries are lossy and the bulk keeps returning.
distractor_notes.C: It exhausts the window.
distractor_notes.D: It ignores the evidence.

questions.stem: Two sources report different growth rates and readers must be able to trace claims. How should findings be carried into the report?

options.text: Average the two numbers and cite neither
Keep the higher figure only
Drop both claims to avoid disagreement
Keep each claim linked to its source, and present both values with their sources rather than silently choosing one

questions.explanation: Reliable reports preserve provenance and surface conflicts.

distractor_notes.A: It fabricates a figure and loses provenance.
distractor_notes.B: It hides the conflict.
distractor_notes.C: It throws away evidence readers need.

questions.stem: In the review job Claude must never write outside `tests/`. That is a policy, not something to leave to the model. What enforces it?

options.text: A Skill explaining the restriction
A CLAUDE.md line limiting edits to `tests/`
A PreToolUse hook on edit and write tools that blocks paths outside `tests/` with exit code 2
A PostToolUse hook that deletes stray files afterwards

questions.explanation: Pre-execution hooks enforce business rules deterministically.

distractor_notes.A: Skills load at the model's discretion.
distractor_notes.B: Advisory only.
distractor_notes.D: The write has already happened.

questions.stem: If the CI job crashes midway, the PR must not look silently approved. What design ensures a sensible end state?

options.text: A wrapper that always posts a final status and, if no complete review exists, posts "review incomplete: human review required"
Re-run the job forever until it passes
Leave the PR without a comment
A prompt telling the model to always finish

questions.explanation: Guarantee an end state in the orchestration layer.

distractor_notes.B: It can block the pipeline and hide the problem.
distractor_notes.C: It reads as no findings.
distractor_notes.D: It cannot help if the process crashes.

questions.stem: Generated tests must always be linted and formatted, independent of whether the model remembers. What implements that?

options.text: A PostToolUse hook on `Edit|Write` that runs the formatter and linter and exits with code 2 with errors on stderr
A `/lint` command developers should remember to run
A CLAUDE.md checklist
A PreToolUse hook that lints the file before it is written

questions.explanation: PostToolUse runs after the edit; exit code 2 returns failures to Claude.

distractor_notes.B: It depends on people remembering.
distractor_notes.C: It is advisory.
distractor_notes.D: The new content does not exist yet.

questions.stem: The generated tests miss null-input edge cases. What is the most effective way to steer the next attempt?

options.text: Start a new session without the earlier output
Ask for more tests without details
Tell Claude the tests are bad
Give one or two concrete example tests showing the desired edge-case style and name the specific cases missing

questions.explanation: Concrete examples and targeted feedback drive refinement.

distractor_notes.A: It loses the context of what was tried.
distractor_notes.B: It may produce more of the same.
distractor_notes.C: It gives no direction.

questions.stem: Besides the blocking PR check, the team wants a nightly review of 5,000 old PRs with no deadline. Which processing mode fits each?

options.text: Batches for the PR check, synchronous for the backlog
Synchronous for both
Synchronous Messages API for the blocking PR check; the asynchronous Message Batches API for the nightly backlog
Batches for both

questions.explanation: Choose by latency need: blocking workflows are synchronous; latency-tolerant bulk work suits batches.

distractor_notes.A: The modes are reversed.
distractor_notes.B: It costs more than needed for work with no deadline.
distractor_notes.D: The PR check blocks a developer and needs a prompt answer.

questions.stem: A script parses the review output as an array of findings and fails on any malformed reply. Which is most reliable?

options.text: Prefill the reply with `[`
A tool whose input schema is the findings array, forced with `tool_choice`
Repair broken output with regexes
Ask for "valid JSON only" in the prompt

questions.explanation: Schema-backed tool use is the most reliable structured output method.

distractor_notes.A: It does not enforce the item schema.
distractor_notes.C: Brittle.
distractor_notes.D: No schema guarantee.

questions.stem: Reviewers keep flagging false positives about `TODO` comments. How should the team use that feedback?

options.text: Tell reviewers to ignore those comments
Remove the review step
Capture each false positive in a structured record (finding type, reviewer verdict, reason) and use the pattern to adjust instructions or add few-shot examples
Raise the temperature to vary findings

questions.explanation: Structured feedback capture feeds prompt and example improvements.

distractor_notes.A: It leaves the cause unaddressed.
distractor_notes.B: It discards the value.
distractor_notes.D: It does not target the recurring error.
